questions.stem: What is the equation for speed?
questions.explanation: Speed is calculated by dividing the distance travelled by the time taken: v = d/t.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes velocity?

options.text: The distance travelled per unit time
The rate of change of acceleration
The total distance divided by total displacement

questions.explanation: Velocity is displacement per unit time. Unlike speed, velocity is a vector quantity that includes direction.

questions.stem: A car travels 150 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time = 150 km / 2 h = 75 km/h.

questions.stem: To convert a speed of 72 km/h into m/s, you should:
questions.explanation: To convert km/h to m/s, divide by 3.6. So 72 km/h / 3.6 = 20 m/s.

questions.stem: What does a car's speedometer show?
questions.explanation: A speedometer shows the instantaneous speed -- the speed at that particular moment. It does not show direction, so it is speed rather than velocity.

questions.stem: An object moves at a constant speed of 5 m/s for 20 seconds. What distance does it travel?
questions.explanation: Distance = speed x time = 5 m/s x 20 s = 100 m.

questions.stem: Why can a moving object have a constant speed but a changing velocity?

options.text: Because velocity depends on mass as well as speed
Because velocity includes direction, which can change even if speed stays the same
Because velocity is always greater than speed
Because speed and velocity are the same thing

questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector that includes direction. If the direction changes (e.g. going around a bend), the velocity changes even if the speed remains constant.
